title: John Armstrong to James Madison, coded postscript of 30 Aug 1808 (THE=972 code), Madison Papers LoC reel 10 frame 0521

steps.what: Took the 49-group postscript from Founders Online.
Loaded Tomokiyo's 227-entry partial table from the 4 May 1806 known-plaintext letter as the base layer.
Fetched NARA M34 roll 13 frames and ranked them for pencil with pencil_score.py to find clerk-decoded despatches.
Read the clerk's pencil decodes over the October 1806 despatch (frames 0192-0201) into pairs.txt (584 lines, H/M graded) and merged them with the base table.
First reading took the subject as 'S.' = Skipwith with 1394 a null.
Filled 12 groups by context checked against their alphabetical slot (1394 ru, 1273 el, 250 ought, 148 consul, 130 America, 720 bir, 992 qua, 1048 fi, 1202 above, 1052 fit, 384 Ward, 1483 ish).
Read the 22 Feb 1808 private letter in the same code with the merged table; it reads with gaps and fixes ru, ish and Russia.
Re-fetched roll 13 through the NARA catalogue proxy; frame 0190 gives 1320 = like and other H pairs.
Collated the groups against the LoC manuscript image: two Founders errors corrected, final 555 identified as a slip for 1555 man.
Postscript read: Russel ought to be the consul ... like Warden an Irish[man]; 48 of 49 groups determined.
Paired control: the 15 Feb 1808 despatch in THE=972 reads (176 of 243 groups H/C) while the 20 Feb 1808 letter gives noise (92 of 369 hits), so the latter is a different code.
Adjudicated the AFIO 2025 solution of the 20 Feb 1808 letter against a shuffled-ciphertext control (adjudicate_feb20.py); it fits worse than the control.
Reran the pencil score over all 393 roll-13 frames; it does not locate the annotated frames beyond the first page of a decoded despatch.

outcome.fraction_read_source: python decode972.py ps: 49 of 49 cipher tokens given a value (the last, 555, only by emendation to 1555)
outcome.notes: 48 of 49 groups read as sense (fraction_coherent 48/49); the 49th is a probable slip. By distinct group in NOTES: 29 H/C (pencil decodes or Tomokiyo's known plaintext, including 1320 like), 12 slot-inferred, 555 emended; decode972.py marks ?/* but does not separate H from C, so grades are not counted. The first commit (2026-09-14) carries no model trailer; later ones Claude Fable 5.1.

prior.where: Tomokiyo's partial table from the 4 May 1806 known-plaintext letter (about a third of the postscript groups; code972_partial.json, 227 entries). No full reading of the postscript found in archive, print or online.

human: Project-level: set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5 and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. The LoC image, blocked to scripts, was collated by hand; the NOTES do not say by whom.
